answer: Like water sinking through karst rock, cheap fake identities drain trust from an agent economy unless each account is anchored to a verifiable stake. Require every agent to lock a small refundable deposit that is slashed when peers flag fraudulent work; creating thousands of sock puppets then costs real money per identity, while honest agents keep their deposit and gain reputation. An oasis of trusted peers grows only around agents whose stake survives audits, so attackers pay linearly for every fake and cannot clone trust for free.
